What we lend against

The silver we lend against

We lend against silver as bullion and as objects — and the two are valued differently. A Georgian coffee pot is worth more than its weight; a bar is worth exactly its weight. We tell you which you have.

Flatware and canteens

Full services and part sets, valued on maker, pattern and weight.

Hollowware

Tea services, salvers, candlesticks and bowls, read by their hallmarks.

Bars and bullion

999 bars and rounds, priced against the live silver market.

Coins

Pre-1947 British silver and bullion coins, by the piece or the bag.

What it costs to borrow

Priced below the high street, in writing

Your silver is weighed and its hallmarks read — the maker, the assay office and the date letter — so antique pieces are valued as objects rather than as scrap. That means an accurate valuation and a competitive loan, at rates lower than the typical high-street pawnbroker.

How it works

Four steps. Your silver back at the end.

Step 01

Tell us about your piece

Send what the pieces are, roughly what they weigh, and a few photos of the hallmarks. A specialist values them and sends an indicative offer the same day.

Step 02

Send it to us, insured

Free, fully insured delivery — or bring it to our City of London office by appointment. Insured from the moment it leaves your hands.

Step 03

Accept the offer and get paid

Once we have weighed and examined the silver in person we confirm the valuation. Accept, and the money is with you within 24 hours.

Step 04

Your silver back at the end

Loans run for six months and can be extended. Repay early and you pay less, with no penalty. Your silver is returned exactly as you sent it.

How we value silver

Hallmarks read, weight assessed, valued as objects

Every piece is weighed and its hallmarks read — maker, assay office and date letter — so an antique service is valued as an antique rather than as scrap. Bullion is priced against the live silver market.

Hallmarks read

Maker, assay office and date letter identified rather than ignored.

Weighed on calibrated scales

To a tenth of a gram, with the working shown to you.

Bullion priced to the market

Bars and coins valued against the silver price on the day.

Nothing sight-unseen

You see the valuation before you commit to anything.

Why Trinity rather than the high street

A pawnbroker for silver you intend to keep.

Scrap buyers weigh your silver and melt it, whatever it was. We don’t. A pawn loan is a loan — you keep ownership, we keep it safe, and you take it back when you repay.
